items.name: init
items.summary: Create a new WebFluent project

options.name: --locales, -l LOCALES
options.meaning: Start it translated: the locales, comma-separated, the default first ("en,ar"). Every visible string goes through t(), and src/translations/ holds a file for each. spa and static only

items.name: build
items.summary: Build the project (compile .wf files to HTML + CSS + JS)
items.writes: the site, in the output folder

options.name: --stats
options.meaning: Print what the build weighs: every file, gzipped, and the runtime modules it kept and left out

options.name: --format FORMAT
options.meaning: How findings are written: `human` (default), `json`, `sarif` (code scanning) or `github` (annotations on a pull request)

options.name: --deny-warnings
options.meaning: Let a warning stop the build as an error does

options.name: --cache
options.meaning: Reuse what earlier builds rendered, kept in `.wf-cache/build/`: only the pages an edit changed are rendered again

options.name: --studio
options.meaning: For an editor's preview: stamp every element with its node id (`data-wf-node`) and write `nodes.json`, from each id to its source

options.name: --allow-output-outside
options.meaning: Let `build.output` name a directory outside the project; without it a build writes only inside the project

items.name: check
items.summary: Check the project — every finding a build would report — and write nothing

options.name: --format FORMAT
options.meaning: How findings are written: `human` (default), `json`, `sarif` (code scanning) or `github` (annotations on a pull request)

options.name: --allow-output-outside
options.meaning: Accept a `build.output` outside the project, as `wf build --allow-output-outside` does; without it the check reports what the build would refuse

items.name: config
items.summary: Read and change `webfluent.app.json`: every setting, what the project sets, and an edit that keeps the file's shape

subcommands.name: schema
subcommands.summary: Every setting: its type, its default and what it does

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.summary: What the project sets at PATH, or the default

subcommands.name: set
subcommands.summary: Set PATH to VALUE — JSON, or a word as a string — keeping the file's shape

options.name: VALUE
options.meaning: The value: JSON (`true`, `3`, `["en", "ar"]`), or a word, which is taken as a string

subcommands.name: unset
subcommands.summary: Remove PATH, so its default applies

items.name: motion
items.summary: The animations an element can play, the eases and speeds, the route transitions and the project's default

items.name: context
items.summary: What an agent is given: the files, the open file, the problems, the components, the theme, the config with only its public env, the guide, and what was withheld

options.name: --open OPEN
options.meaning: The file open in the editor, and its selection as byte offsets: `src/pages/Home.wf` or `src/pages/Home.wf:120-180`

options.name: --guide GUIDE
options.meaning: The guide as its chapters' sections (`index`) or whole (`full`) (default `index`)

options.name: --json
options.meaning: Print JSON, for tools; otherwise one Markdown document

items.name: translations
items.summary: The translations as a table: each locale's plural forms and what it lacks, each key's messages, and where a `t()` names it

options.name: --missing MISSING
options.meaning: Only the keys this locale has no message for

options.name: --plurals
options.meaning: CLDR's plural rules instead: every locale's forms, and the form each of a run of counts takes

items.name: scope
items.summary: What a path picker lists at a place: the names in scope there, each with its type and where it comes from, and the fields to go on into

options.name: --data DATA
options.meaning: A template's data, a JSON file, to list after the scope

items.name: rules
items.summary: The rules a `validate` block may hold, the named patterns, when a form shows its messages, and every state the project holds to a rule

items.name: theme
items.summary: The theme the build uses: every token, declared or inherited, where each is used, and its contrast pairs

items.name: components
items.summary: Every component a call can name — the built-ins and the project's — with what each takes: its props and their kinds, events, slots, parts and children

items.name: assets
items.summary: What `public/` holds — each file's kind, size and dimensions, and where the project names it — or what the media pipeline will make of one image

options.name: --plan PATH
options.meaning: What the pipeline will make of this image of `public/`: `/hero.png`

items.name: commands
items.summary: Every `wf` command, its options and what it writes, as data

items.name: fix
items.summary: Fix every finding that has a fix — or every one of a code — as `wf check` and the editor offer it, and say what is left

options.name: --dry-run
options.meaning: Write nothing; say what would change

items.name: explain
items.summary: What a diagnostic code means, a program that draws it, and the fix; with no code, every code

options.name: --json
options.meaning: Print JSON, for tools: one code, or every code without one

items.name: serve
items.summary: Start the development server
items.writes: the site, in the output folder, on every save

options.name: --host HOST
options.meaning: The address to listen on: this machine only by default; `0.0.0.0` lets a phone on the same network reach it

options.name: --allow-output-outside
options.meaning: Let `build.output` name a directory outside the project

items.name: generate
items.summary: Generate a new page, component, or store

options.name: KIND
options.meaning: What to generate: page, component, or store

options.name: NAME
options.meaning: Name of the item to generate

items.name: render
items.summary: Render a .wf template with JSON data

options.name: TEMPLATE
options.meaning: Template file (.wf or .wfx), or a directory: every template under it as one, components shared

options.name: --data DATA
options.meaning: JSON data file (reads stdin if omitted)

options.name: --theme THEME
options.meaning: Which `Theme` declared in the template to render with. Only needed when the template declares more than one

options.name: --token NAME=VALUE
options.meaning: A design token over the theme's, `NAME=VALUE`; may be given more than once

options.name: --page PAGE
options.meaning: The page to render, by name, when the template has several

options.name: --lang LANG
options.meaning: The document's language, `<html lang>` (default: the page's `lang:`, else `en`)

items.name: migrate
items.summary: Carry a project forward: WebFluent 2 sources to the current grammar, then a 3 project to what 4 allows

options.name: [PATH]
options.meaning: Project directory (default: current directory), or one .wf file

options.name: --check
options.meaning: Report what would change without writing anything

options.name: --stdout
options.meaning: Print the migrated text of one file to stdout instead of writing it

options.name: --wfx
options.meaning: Write the migrated files in the indented layout, as `.wfx`

items.name: docs
items.summary: Write a component gallery: every built-in, and what the project declares
items.writes: a gallery, in the folder `--out` names

items.name: test
items.summary: Run the project's `test "…" { … }` declarations under tests/

options.name: [PATH]
options.meaning: Project directory (default: current directory), or one test file

options.name: --update
options.meaning: Rewrite every snapshot with the current render

items.name: audit
items.summary: What this project trusts: markup it did not write, other origins, what it keeps on the reader's machine, its `env` names, its policy and its dependencies

items.name: verify
items.summary: Load every page of a built project in a real browser: errors, failed requests, paint timing, and which built-ins it drew

options.name: --budget MS
options.meaning: Fail a route whose first paint is slower than this, in milliseconds

options.name: --returning-visitor
options.meaning: Visit every route again as a reader whose storage holds what the previous build's pages kept

options.name: --allow-output-outside
options.meaning: Let `build.output` name a directory outside the project

items.name: registry
items.summary: Describe every built-in component: props, cases, flags, events, slots, parts

items.name: types
items.summary: Describe what a project declares: enums, types, components, stores, pages

items.name: fmt
items.summary: Format a project's source files; with `--to`, rewrite them in the other layout: `.wfx` (blocks by indentation) or `.wf` (blocks in braces)

options.name: [PATH]
options.meaning: Project directory (default: current directory), or one file

options.name: --check
options.meaning: Write nothing; fail when a file is not formatted

options.name: --stdout
options.meaning: Print the formatted text to stdout instead of writing it
